## Design

### 2026-10-09 – # DAY 1:

**4h**

# DAY 1:

Today I started my first project for Hackclub HalfLife. Because Meta recently announced an **open Source SDK for the Esp32** for their [AI Muse](https://gadgets.muse.ai/), I thought that it might be cool to build a gadget that uses this sdk.

Even though I'm not fully new to pcb design, I also **wouldn't call myself experienced**. That's why I actually was impressed how easy it was to wire the schematic.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/57hiQNAgkNbxG5Q8GjhzMk9nORrt5I37/82603bc975c1965985569b388281a8b46e5991249c274dd056bc2e4b2064842f.png)

One small problem I had was that I **couldn't find any SH1106 librarys for KiCad** but luckily I could just use a generic Interface Symbol with VCC, GND, SDA and SCL.

I also assigned the footprints to the symbols, which actually was kinda challenging because I had to import the Library for the xiao esp32

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/57hiQNAgkNbxG5Q8GjhzMk9nORrt5I37/cf05ab51f927bc6cfc65a377beaeba51a79a2014ec0279a32df6e36721623939.png)

This is the finished result now in the PCB-Editor. YIPPIIEEH 🥳🥳🥳:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/57hiQNAgkNbxG5Q8GjhzMk9nORrt5I37/bb066cef3231be00efd1348076d8c85909e09d5d890aa7f62d8dd4b754229020.png)

Before I start the next steps of the design I wanted to **brainstorm a bit on the form factor**. Here's a small drawing I drew to brainstorm ideas:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/57hiQNAgkNbxG5Q8GjhzMk9nORrt5I37/e850334c18475ea3e8193a737b35c919c389fb1301f05fe02a22a3ea8d671dd9.png)

Overall I am pretty happy with my progress and I am looking forward to **the next design steps**

### 2026-10-10 – # DAY 2:

**2.5h**

# DAY 2:

Today I **started laying out the pcb.** First things first I drew the outline of the pcb. For this I used a reference Image. The biggest challenge here was understanding how draw curves with the available kicad tools. After tinkering around a bit I came up with a result I liked. (I also tried to make the design **as symmetrical as possible.**)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/57hiQNAgkNbxG5Q8GjhzMk9nORrt5I37/c40b7a93b157bd301ee768a7a8cf85fd05353f6707d020aa4fae97dcdb642756.png)

Also this was my reference Image:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/57hiQNAgkNbxG5Q8GjhzMk9nORrt5I37/ae86865fe27e651692e0635887a8b864bce797c633ef40c9c45074d276a09799.png)

Next step was to roughly lay out the components on the pcb. I decided that the screen should be **the face of the "muse"**.  Later on into the project it can display little eyes that change at different events. This is the **pre-final layout.** (Maybe I am going to change it later on)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/57hiQNAgkNbxG5Q8GjhzMk9nORrt5I37/786ffe95959cffa4231cdb4fb01d611e16aa1e152b6fcda1b78a3a0a812c080c.png)

Overall this was a short but productive session. Looking forward I am going to **wire everything up** and finish up the githup project. :)

### 2026-10-10 – # DAY 3:

**2.5h**

# DAY 3:

Today I wired up all the components of PCB. The callenging part of this task was to make a clean and simple **2-layer pcb-design.** Therefore I spent quite some time changing up the wires to create **a polished end-product.**

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/57hiQNAgkNbxG5Q8GjhzMk9nORrt5I37/6edad106417844a142ea2740c2f61c6335d17e1aa5f569525adc265610121f33.png)

After that I drew some silkscreen lines for decoration and started adding symbols and logos **to personalize my design:**

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/57hiQNAgkNbxG5Q8GjhzMk9nORrt5I37/706b0eebaaa5d3d281d39db1ea8e916772bb1a201070dd888ca03ae8f5159d7b.png)

After refining my design for a bit I came up with a finished design, which in exported from kicad and **uploaded to my github repo.**

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/57hiQNAgkNbxG5Q8GjhzMk9nORrt5I37/a54413443de73523f4a4b1b3c0ba7d622baa6e18d880f764992effc5e59f4302.png)

Overall I am pretty happy about how the pcb turned out. Next up I am going to work **on the firmware.**

### 2026-10-10 – # DAY 4:

**2h**

# DAY 4:

After I finished the pcb-design I worked on the repo and **finished up the firmware.** As I am  more or less fully new to git cloning and custom firmwares that was pretty intense.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/57hiQNAgkNbxG5Q8GjhzMk9nORrt5I37/9804fdf6adb5c2ec9b1ac5519613cfc2f13304009dc04cb4293afb48c481f905.png)

## The key problems I had where:
- the tutorial I followed always mentioned Linux & MacOS but no Windows
- I couldn't really extend and hack the firmware because I would need to test it out beforehand (I will add extra feautures later in the build part
- theoretical firmware design without a practical testing area is kinda hard :)

But after ** back and forth between the console and the tutorial** I eventually got it to work.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/57hiQNAgkNbxG5Q8GjhzMk9nORrt5I37/96a28189b676c15d08a92981c3dd82937a6daf66d66efaecf6b3b25b6e4959d4.png)

Last but not least I wrote a nice repo **and finished my first Half-Life-Project!!! YIPPIEH 🥳🥳🥳**
